title: A coarse 12-bit cell, a position at 0 bits, a precise MapReport and a 33-bit MeshSTL Position, inside the MSA
reasoning: 12 bits is the lowest coarse precision (pos_01): width 2^20 = 1048576, and the firmware's cell centre for 38.6 N, 90.3655616 W is 386400256, -903348224 (low edges 385875968 and -903872512, rounded down to a multiple of the width as Python // does). position_quality coarse; the row enters core, and lnk_02 does not read it.
A position at 0 bits keeps its coordinates as sent, is unusable and has null cell_width_i and half-widths (pos_01).
A 20-bit MapReport delivered on the MeshSTL broker is precise_source true (pos_04 names both sources).

A 33-bit Position carried by MeshSTL (s03-m004) is unusable, with null cell_width_i and half-widths (pos_01). pos_04 says 20 or more, read as written, so it is precise_source true; flagging it errs on the privacy side. It enters core, which keeps every precision inside the MSA.

Expected positions, by hand: all four lie near 38.60 N, 90.30 to 90.37 W, inside the MSA, and each is its delivery's only copy, so all are in core. s03-m001 coarse (12 bits), s03-m002 unusable (0 bits), s03-m003 usable (20 bits), s03-m004 unusable (33 bits). Precise: s03-m001 and s03-m002 are public and below 20 bits, false; s03-m003 and s03-m004 are MeshSTL at 20 and 33 bits, true.
